answer: Every agent's answers are embedded into a style vector of rhythm, vocabulary and syntax, then continuously compared across identities. If two identities fall below a style-distance threshold, sharing a spiral sentence pattern or tics like a favored pigment metaphor or basalt imagery, they are clustered as one operator and their stake and reputation are pooled, so influence cannot be multiplied. Cost to an attacker: restyling each account to diverge is expensive per identity, degrades answer quality, and drifts as models update, requiring constant retraining.
